cells.tense: You are here, with your attention on the one direction you have chosen.
cells.act: defend the direction you chose against the next push
cells.ask: When something pulls you toward drifting, stay with the practice you chose and watch the pull go by un-followed once.
cells.core:
You are moving in one direction with something, and the practice that keeps it alive is one you actually keep. Not many things, not scattered — this one. It grows because you come back to it. On its good days the direction comes from genuine engagement: you stay with what you care about, and the staying is what makes it real.

What keeps this going is that you defend the chosen direction against the next push off course. The next time a pull comes — a distraction, a doubt, a better-sounding alternative — hold the line once. Return to the practice instead of following the pull. That is the whole act, small enough to do without anyone's help. The practice keeps its shape because you keep choosing it, one return at a time.
cells.sheetLine: The practice holds because you return to it.
cells.verb: merging into one direction with what you chose
cells.place: where you keep the practice by repeating it

cells.tense: You will be braced for the next intrusion before it even arrives.
cells.ask: Sit with one finished thing the practice has built — a page, a set, a piece — for ten minutes, adding nothing.
cells.core:
You are bracing against a future you cannot write yet, and the practice has turned into control. Every session aims at what comes next, so nothing you have made is allowed to be finished; finishing would mean stopping. On its good days the direction comes from genuine engagement, not from force. The care stays; the clutching is what grew around it.

Care has another half: taking pleasure in the result. Take one thing the practice has already made and sit with it — read it, listen to it, look at it — and give it ten minutes of your attention, nothing added. Something built this slowly is allowed to be seen. The grip costs you; resting in the result is how you set it down.
cells.sheetLine: Stop adding long enough to enjoy what is already built.
cells.verb: merging into one direction with what you chose
cells.place: where you keep the practice by repeating it

cells.tense: You were standing at a door that is already behind you.
cells.act: list the pulls on you and mark which are yours
cells.ask: Name every pull on you right now — each direction, each claim — and mark the ones that are actually yours; keep that list a day.
cells.core:
The practice has been running on empty. You keep it by repetition, but repetition alone — no genuine engagement getting in, no result being allowed to matter — is now a chore. The connection you chose is not feeding the practice. Where this sits well, imagining flows from integration: you dream out of what you have lived, not to get away from it.

The way through is not more effort in the practice. Name the pulls on you — every direction, every claim, each one set down with no verdict about which is right — and mark the ones that are actually yours. Stay with that for a day. That is the act, and the energy comes through seeing, not through pushing the starved practice harder.
cells.sheetLine: The practice runs on empty because nothing new is reaching it.
cells.verb: merging into one direction with what you chose
cells.place: where you keep the practice by repeating it

cells.tense: You are already writing, and the pen is still down in your own hand.
cells.act: show someone the way you found
cells.ask: Take one person through the route you found on a problem you actually solved. Walk it with them once, then let them go on alone.
cells.core:
You are steering by a kind of knowing you do not credit. The practice is held — you come back to it, you refine it — and you call the staying habit, the direction whatever you happen to be doing lately. You are the one defending the chosen line, and you would say it is just how the work goes. Where this sits well, the practice flows without force and the refining serves the work rather than your worry.

Showing that route to someone is how it comes back to you. Take one person through it, walk the path with them once, and then let them go on alone. That is the act, and it is yours the moment you do it. Showing the passage makes an author visible, and the author is already there.
cells.sheetLine: You found the route. Show it to someone and it is yours.
cells.verb: merging into one direction with what you chose
cells.place: where you keep the practice by repeating it

attempts.check: The record supports a chosen connection and a practice built by repetition; it does not say who the reader is merging with or what the practice is. A reader could reasonably say the merging is with a person, a craft, or an idea — I keep the act on the practice itself so the read survives all three. The asks stay useful if my read is wrong because each is a small experiment the reader can run and judge by what they notice. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'two streams, one flow' — the record's lyric, and I have kept it off the glass.
